Gate B blocker #1: driver OOM on the run-sheet-default n2-standard-2 master (Hail driver killed during query compilation; SparkException 'Could not find CoarseGrainedScheduler' + clean hail.log = OS OOM-kill, not executor loss). FIXED by recreating with an n2-standard-16 master (master size is create-time only). Baked into memory project_aou_dataproc_hail_install MASTER/DRIVER SIZING + runbook.

Gate B blocker #2 (the real query-shape bug): indefinite DRIVER-COLLECT stall in load_qc_cohort. ROOT-CAUSED + FIXED via /gsd-debug (HIGH confidence). Root cause: mt.repartition(2048) (default shuffle=True) right after split_multi_hts + before the post_split checkpoint built a Spark RangePartitioner by sampling row keys across all input partitions; with the partitioner invalidated by split_multi, Hail lowered the boundary computation to a driver-side SpillingCollectIterator (jstack: TableValue.mapRows -> ExecuteRelational), funneling ~2,077 partitions to the master, spilling to /tmp (~38 min, ~1.4s driver CPU, 0 executor threads). Redundant too (naive_coalesce already set count=2048; checkpoint write+reread already yields a clean partitioner). Fix (Hail-team 'repartition after write, not before'): dropped the pre-write repartition; rebalance on the post_split checkpoint READ-BACK via hl.read_matrix_table(ckpt, _n_partitions=_post_split_read_partitions(...)) — on-disk partition index, no key sampling, no driver gather. New pure helper _post_split_read_partitions + constant _COHORT_TARGET_PARTITIONS=2048. 3 RED-first regression guards; tests/m3 112 passed/27 skipped; Track-4 guard _assert_checkpoint_nonempty byte-identical (verified via diff scope). Would also have crippled the full genome-wide fire. LIVE end-to-end proof DEFERRED to the Gate B re-fire.

Surfaces as 'Could not find CoarseGrainedScheduler' + py4j RemoteDisconnected with a CLEAN hail.log. Master size is create-time only.

decisions.decision: load_qc_cohort rebalances on the post_split checkpoint READ-BACK (read_matrix_table _n_partitions), NOT a pre-write mt.repartition(shuffle=True)
decisions.rationale: pre-write repartition(shuffle=True) builds a RangePartitioner by sampling keys across all partitions -> driver-side SpillingCollectIterator gather (the Gate B stall). The Hail core team recommends 'repartition after write, not before' / _n_partitions on read, which uses the on-disk partition index (no key sampling, no driver collect). Tradeoff accepted: read-back rebalances partition COUNT not SIZES; even-sizing now comes from naive_coalesce alone (fine for Spark; the Hail-recommended pattern for heavily-filtered MTs).
